promptAsSent:
Use the image_gen tool to generate exactly one image, then stop. Do not write files, run commands or edit anything.

Attached reference images, in order:
Image 1: Geometry authority: exact silhouettes, layout, placement and scale; flat colours are placeholders, not material
Image 2: Family and identity: the accepted derelict walker of this line (its material, plating, colour, detail and part language); not this machine's layout or design
Image 3: Material and rendering style only (vanilla derelict_rampart, 4x Lanczos); not layout or subject

Game sprite sheet for a top-down tactical game: an unpiloted Domain-era derelict WALKER of the same machine line as reference image 2 (the accepted security walker, the 'sentinel'): it must read as the same family and maker, its own build at its own size, never a recolour or copy of it. No cockpit, canopy or pilot.

Reference image 1 is the GEOMETRY AUTHORITY (a grey block-in). Keep its layout exactly: on the LEFT the whole walker assembled, the torso in the middle and four legs reaching out in an X; on the RIGHT the same machine's parts drawn apart, upright: the torso alone (top), one thigh segment (bottom left: hip joint at its lower end, knee end at its top) and one shin segment (bottom right: knee joint at its lower end, a heavy three-toed clamp foot at its top). Keep every part's position, size, outline and orientation as in the guide, so the parts can be cut out by their boxes; keep the gaps between parts empty. The torso on the right must be the same design as on the left, and every leg on the left uses the parts on the right.

DESIGN: a HAULER, an unarmed load-carrying walker: a broad, heavy body whose back is one deep open load bed (a hopper with plated sides) carrying stripped scrap metal (torn plates, girder ends, wreck parts), a small rounded sensor head forward of it, a power pack behind. Thick, planted legs built to carry weight. No guns. 

SURFACE: like image 2 and the vanilla derelict ships (image 3): never smooth, clean, rounded or toy-like. Many small overlapping armour plates with hard bevelled edges and dark seams, exposed machinery, pipes, cable bundles and pistons between plates, rivet rows, vents, dents, scrapes, chipped paint, grime in every recess; dense detail that still reads at sprite scale, crisp edges. COLOUR: sage-green and khaki plate, yellow diagonal hazard bands, bone-white and brass machinery, rust-brown grime, red sensor lamps; the saw discs and cutting edges bare worn steel. Muted, old and gritty. Absolutely no text, letters, numbers, serial numbers, stencils, logos, emblems, insignia or symbols anywhere. 

Strict overhead orthographic view, the camera straight down, the machine facing the TOP of the canvas. Plain flat light grey background (#b4b4b4) everywhere around and between the parts; no ground, no cast shadow, no shadow slab, no border, no labels.
